# Tracktools Benchmark Notes

This file tracks reproducible mainline-generation benchmarks only. Generated track XML, AC files, and OSM caches under `runtime/` remain local artifacts and are not distribution assets.

Run commands from `torcs/torcs/` with the `torcs-tracktools` Conda environment.

`torcs-rebuild-mainline` defaults to the DP-biarc drafter. The current matrix below uses the explicit geometric closure solver (`--closure-solver geometric`) and is the canonical comparison target; the legacy polyline matrix is retained for historical comparison.

## Current DP-Biarc + Geometric Closure Benchmark Status

All listed tracks have `closure-report-mainline.json` with `"ok": true` in the local benchmark runtime tree when generated by DP-biarc plus the geometric terminal-lever closure solver. The current rows are from the sequential `zz-geombench1-*` rerun across every non-`zz-*` road track with a local `source/` directory.

Compared with the prior `zz-dpbench5-*` matrix for the overlapping 10 benchmark tracks, total wall time changed from about `816.5s` to `315.7s`. `road-america` is the only overlapping row that became slower (`43.8s` to `61.2s`) because geometric closure needed four candidate attempts; the other nine rows improved.

The geometric closer's key benchmark finding is that final longitudinal `Delta X` should be corrected by a terminal straight at the end of the loop after `Delta Y` and heading are solved. Start-side X probing and broad alternate-control searches were slower and less reliable in local experiments.

## Reproducible Commands

Current DP-biarc + geometric closure rebuild template:

```powershell
conda run -n torcs-tracktools torcs-rebuild-mainline `
  --input runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/centerline-osm.json `
  --output-track-xml runtime/tracks/road/<name>/<name>.xml `
  --closure-solver geometric `
  --timing-report runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/rebuild-mainline-timing.json
```

Legacy polyline benchmark template for reproducing the matrix above:

```powershell
conda run -n torcs-tracktools torcs-rebuild-mainline `
  --input runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/centerline-osm.json `
  --output-track-xml runtime/tracks/road/<name>/<name>.xml `
  --segment-fitter polyline `
  --timing-report runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/rebuild-mainline-timing-polyline.json
```

Current DP-biarc + geometric closure Le Mans reversed direction:

```powershell
conda run -n torcs-tracktools torcs-rebuild-mainline `
  --input runtime/tracks/road/le-mans/source/centerline-osm.json `
  --output-track-xml runtime/tracks/road/le-mans/le-mans.xml `
  --reverse-input `
  --closure-solver geometric `
  --timing-report runtime/tracks/road/le-mans/source/rebuild-mainline-timing.json
```

Legacy polyline Le Mans reversed direction:

```powershell
conda run -n torcs-tracktools torcs-rebuild-mainline `
  --input runtime/tracks/road/le-mans/source/centerline-osm.json `
  --output-track-xml runtime/tracks/road/le-mans/le-mans.xml `
  --segment-fitter polyline `
  --reverse-input `
  --target-dy 0.001 `
  --timing-report runtime/tracks/road/le-mans/source/rebuild-mainline-timing-polyline.json
```

Manual strict closure fallback for a nearly-closed candidate:

```powershell
conda run -n torcs-tracktools torcs-close-loop `
  --track-xml runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/<candidate>.xml `
  --runtime-dir runtime `
  --category road `
  --name <name> `
  --config runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/closure-config-mainline.json `
  --report runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/closure-report-mainline.json `
  --target-dy 0.001
```

Do not use `torcs-close-loop --profile post-pit` for baseline/no-pit benchmark reruns unless the benchmark set is being explicitly revalidated. The post-pit profile is only for Pit10 start-line rotation closure. The default DP-biarc rebuild path enables `--linear-polish` automatically; legacy polyline benchmark reruns should keep their recorded flags unless intentionally testing the polish path.

## Segment Reduction Targets

Prioritize segment-count reduction where it buys the most maintenance value:

1. `le-mans`: 229 segments, long source with many OSM points; target first for merge/simplification work.
2. `silverstone-gp`: 161 segments, established regression track; useful to detect simplification regressions.
3. `barcelona`: 145 segments from a single OSM way; good test for seam handling and redundant curvature splits.
4. `kyalami`: 143 segments, known-good baseline; use as a stability guard.
5. `imola`: 142 segments, filtered relation source; checks that filtering and simplification remain compatible.

Acceptance for simplification experiments:

- Keep source coverage at or above `0.98`.
- Keep `closure-report-mainline.json` at `"ok": true`.
- Preserve expected race direction and layout choice.
- Avoid track-specific hacks; prefer generic fitter/merge improvements.
- Record any widened closure target such as `--target-dy 0.001`.

## Compact `--min-seg-len 20` Experiments

`--min-seg-len 20` is a validated opt-in compact profile. It reduces segment count across the benchmark set, but it trades lower segment count for larger source-fit deviations and can increase closure search time on some tracks. Keep the default conservative unless a lower-maintenance generated mainline is worth the runtime/fit tradeoff.

Validated local experiments:

| Track | Baseline Segments | Compact Segments | Change | Closure | Time s | Attempts | Flags / Notes |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | --- | ---: | ---: | --- |
| silverstone-gp | 161 | 131 | -19% | ok | 515.1 | 4 | `--min-seg-len 20`; slower than baseline, useful guard |
| kyalami | 143 | 101 | -29% | ok | 256.8 | 1 | `--min-seg-len 20 --target-dy 0.001`; slower than baseline |
| sebring | 124 | 98 | -21% | ok | 154.2 | 1 | `--min-seg-len 20`; slower than baseline |
| imola | 142 | 79 | -44% | ok | 421.8 | 3 | `--min-seg-len 20`; larger fit error but closed |
| daytona-road | 119 | 96 | -19% | ok | 254.2 | 2 | `--min-seg-len 20`; slower than baseline |
| road-america | 132 | 114 | -14% | ok | 180.3 | 1 | `--min-seg-len 20`; much faster than baseline outlier |
| le-mans | 229 | 193 | -16% | ok | 319.6 | 1 | `--min-seg-len 20 --reverse-input --target-dy 0.001`; faster than baseline |
| barcelona | 145 | 87 | -40% | ok | 134.5 | 1 | `--min-seg-len 20`; single-way source remains closable |
| yas-marina | 133 | 111 | -17% | ok | 424.7 | 2 | `--min-seg-len 20`; slower than baseline |
| interlagos | 110 | 81 | -26% | ok | 223.3 | 1 | `--min-seg-len 20`; slightly faster than baseline |

Compact rebuild template:

```powershell
conda run -n torcs-tracktools torcs-rebuild-mainline `
  --input runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/centerline-osm.json `
  --output-track-xml runtime/tracks/road/<name>/<name>.xml `
  --segment-fitter polyline `
  --min-seg-len 20 `
  --timing-report runtime/tracks/road/<name>/source/rebuild-mainline-timing-polyline-min20.json
```

The full guard set closes with this profile. Do not make `20 m` the default without a separate decision, because several stable tracks become slower even though their segment counts improve.
